R-privacy-1 (Phone numbers and names go to a US processor with no transfer safeguard identified) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
A daily job selects the profiles whose birthday is today and posts each
phone number and display name to Textly's API (hosted in the United
States), which sends the message.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Greetings are sent by SMS through Textly
findings.recommendation: Identify Textly as a processor (Art. 28 data processing agreement) and state the Chapter V transfer mechanism (adequacy decision / EU-US Data Privacy Framework certification, or standard contractual clauses), or choose an EEA-hosted SMS provider; record the processing in the Art. 30 register.
findings.title: Phone numbers and names go to a US processor with no transfer safeguard identified

findings.evidence:
kept as long as the profile exists, and copied with the rest of the
database into the nightly backups.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Birth dates live on the profile
findings.recommendation: Tie retention to the opt-in — clear `birthday` and `phone` when the member opts out or the profile is deleted — and state the backup retention period after which erased values are gone from backups (Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation).
findings.title: Birthday and phone are kept for the profile's lifetime, including after opt-out, and in backups with no expiry

findings.evidence: The profile form SHALL offer birthday greetings as an option, off by default; a member who opts in SHALL give their birthday (day and month) and a mobile phone number.
findings.location: specs/birthday-greetings/spec.md#Requirement: Members opt in to birthday greetings
findings.recommendation: Add a requirement and scenarios for withdrawing consent (opting out stops greetings and erases `birthday` and `phone`, Art. 7(3) and Art. 17), and state that access and export of the profile include the two new fields (Art. 15, Art. 20); add matching tasks.
findings.title: No requirement for opting out or erasing the new data

findings.evidence: Members enjoy being remembered; marketing wants birthday messages.
findings.recommendation: Question for the team — state the purpose (sending the birthday greeting only, or also marketing) and the lawful basis (consent via the opt-in, Art. 6(1)(a)); if marketing messages are intended, the SMS needs ePrivacy-compliant consent for direct marketing and the purpose must be disclosed at opt-in.
findings.title: Purpose and lawful basis of the new data are not stated

findings.location: design.md#Decision: Greetings are sent by SMS through Textly
findings.recommendation: Send only the phone number and a generic message, or state why the personalised name is needed (Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation).
findings.title: Display name is sent to Textly where the phone number alone would do

findings.evidence: - [Textly is down] → the job retries the next day.
findings.recommendation: State that the job and its retry logic log only the profile id, never the phone number, birthday or name, nor Textly's request body.
findings.title: No rule keeps phone numbers out of the job's logs and retry state
